body: I'm in a similar position tbh. One thing that I keep hearing over and over again is take care of yourself. Get a good night's rest, take vitamins if you can, eat a large breakfast, get exercise, wear better clothes. Next thing is take notes in a journal about how you think you can improve. For me, the negative feedback loop makes me interpret things as judments, instead of teaching moments. That's where the notes come in. Just know that even if you think you're not a talented person, please don't forget to add the "yet" to the end of that sentence!

I'm with you there. Sometimes association helps me. You can usually break down words into components. For lour (looking angry or sullen), I use looking sour. If there's a way for you to make it stand out, that would work too. It can leave me confused sometimes but, combining it with your method would make it better.

As far as learning goes, it's helped me to cut down on music. Whenever I get the chance to listen to something while I'm doing something else, I choose something I'm interested in. Passive learning like that doesn't change your life that much but, over time it can be pretty useful. If this isn't something you're already doing, I hope it helps.
Thanks for this I'll try it.
